title: Basic Architecture: Layers and Responsibilities
learningObjectives: Describe architecture as organizing responsibilities and boundaries.
Explain a simple layered arrangement of user interface, logic, and data access.
Identify why layers should depend on clear interfaces.
Recognize when layering adds unnecessary complexity.
Trace a request through a simple layered design.

understand.concept: Architecture organizes a system's major responsibilities and the relationships between them. A simple layered design may separate user interface, application or domain logic, and data access. The UI gathers input and presents results; logic applies rules; data access reads or writes storage. Layers communicate through defined interfaces rather than reaching into each other's internals. Small applications may not need formal layers, but boundaries become useful when complexity, change, or testing needs justify them.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear design boundaries and intentional development practices help teams maintain software, verify changes, and respond to real needs.
understand.analogy: Think of a team coordinating a shared task: clear responsibilities and feedback loops help everyone work toward the same result.
understand.analogyLimit: Software design includes precise technical constraints and interactions that teamwork analogies cannot fully represent.

explain.narrative: A request can flow from UI to logic to a data adapter and return a result for display. Keeping business rules out of presentation code allows those rules to be tested without a screen. Keeping storage details behind an adapter makes it easier to replace a data source. Avoid layers that only forward calls without adding a useful boundary.

examples.title: Avoid a useless forwarding layer

commonMistakes: Treating design smells as automatic defects.
Overengineering small projects with unnecessary layers or patterns.
Mixing requirements, features, and refactoring without clear intent.
Ignoring tests or edge cases when changing structure.
Failing to consider project context and trade-offs.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: Sketch a small app's UI, rules, and storage responsibilities. Trace one user action through the responsibilities. Move one rule out of presentation code if needed. Define what each layer receives and returns. Explain which boundary adds value and which would be unnecessary.

independentTask.instructions: Plan a simple notes or expense-record app. Identify UI, logic, and data responsibilities. Draw or describe the flow for creating one record. Define one interface between logic and storage. Explain how the design supports testing and future change without excessive layers.
